title: Whether the freeze holds against an agent that switches off the project's own record-keeping
situation: Under 0129 the project's history refuses at a hook every change to a branch passes. An agent's own shell can switch the project's hooks off for one command (pointing the hooks folder elsewhere, the hook manager's off switch, or deleting the hook), as it can set its own name (0130); the commit then enters its local history unrefused. Only a history the agent does not hold, the one shared through the remote and guarded by the project's gates workflow, is out of its reach, and that guard needs to know who made each commit.
decision: Recommended: the freeze holds at the project's own record-keeping as the project runs it; an agent that switches that record-keeping off is breaching the project's tooling, which the freeze does not claim to hold against in an agent's local history. Holding it in the shared history needs each commit to carry its agent in a form the gates workflow can judge, a separate cut together with 0130.
consequences: Accepted, examples 31 to 33 and 36 hold wherever the project's record-keeping runs, and a commit made with it switched off is outside the freeze. Rejected, the freeze extends to the shared history, a realization beyond this cut, and the cut does not complete until it is built.
